label: Heavy rail retained to Newcastle station
purpose: Primary counterfactual: the line is not cut
notes: Modernised frequency and interchange, not the 2014 service as-is (proposal s9, counterfactual naivety). Hunter St retains the road capacity and kerbside parking that the tram removed.

label: Bus shuttle from Wickham, no light rail
purpose: The December 2012 policy as originally announced

label: Light rail as built (wire-free, current signals)
purpose: Actual. The reference case for every comparison
notes: Charging dwell 20 s per intermediate stop; no transit signal priority.

label: Light rail, charging dwell removed
purpose: Isolates the wire-free decision (secondary question S-a)
notes: dwell_charging_s set to 0 at all stops; everything else identical to S2.

label: Light rail with full transit signal priority
notes: Green extension plus early start at all 14 corridor intersections; 75 per cent of tram signal delay removed.

label: Light rail on the Option A alignment
purpose: The route with plurality public support that was not selected
notes: Reserved former-railway alignment: 60 km/h line speed, few at-grade conflicts, and Hunter Street keeps its road capacity.

label: Bus rapid transit on the same alignment
purpose: The alternative the 2020 Strategic Business Case later favoured
notes: Same 6 stops and same lane take as the tram; 7.5 minute headway.

label: Light rail extended to Broadmeadow
notes: Adds Hamilton and Broadmeadow; corridor length rises from 2.7 to 5.2 km.

label: Light rail to Broadmeadow and John Hunter Hospital
purpose: Upper bound of the plausible network
notes: Adds Lambton and John Hunter Hospital; corridor length about 9.5 km.

label: No trunk mode; walk, cycle and local bus only
notes: Light rail removed and not replaced.
